headline: Phillies rally past Marlins, stretch win streak to five
recap: The Phillies beat the Marlins 6-4 at Citizens Bank Park on Tuesday. Miami stretched its lead to 3-1 in the top of the sixth inning, but Philadelphia answered right back, scoring four runs in the bottom half on a two-run double from Alec Bohm and a two-run single from Bryson Stott to take a 5-3 lead. Michael Petersen took the loss after allowing all four of those runs; Alex McFarlane (1-1) picked up the win with a scoreless inning, and Brooks Raley closed it out for his first save. Starter Zack Wheeler worked five innings, allowing two runs on two hits with seven strikeouts.
The win pushed Philadelphia to 69-58, 5.5 games behind the first-place Atlanta Braves in the NL East, and extended the team's winning streak to five games.

The Phillies close out their series with the Marlins on Wednesday night at Citizens Bank Park, with Aaron Nola facing Miami's Sandy Alcantara; first pitch is scheduled for 6:05 PM ET. DraftKings lists the Phillies as -123 favorites on the moneyline. An off day follows Thursday before the Phillies open a three-game series at home against the St. Louis Cardinals on Friday.
